ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a semicircular dial, with 10 marked at the left end and 11 marked at the right end; there are several thicker intermediate tick marks on the arc. A black pointer points from near the center of the circle toward the upper left, and the arrow tip falls near the first subdivision close to the 10 side, overall still clearly in the small range after increasing to the right from 10. Reasoning: Treat 10 to 11 as a scale that increases uniformly along the semicircular arc, and make an approximate linear reading according to the subdivisions in the figure. The arrow position is not far from 10, about a part of the interval from 10 to the next subdivision, estimated to be about 0.15 greater than 10. Therefore the reading indicated by the arrow is about 10.15.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a semicircular scale: the left end is labeled 10, the right end is labeled 11, and the intermediate tick marks divide the arc into equal parts, so the upper-left tick corresponds to about 10.25. The arrow tip lies between the 10 mark and the 10.25 tick, noticeably closer to 10.25 than to 10 but still before that tick. Estimate its position by linear interpolation along that first quarter interval: it is roughly 0.15 above 10, giving an approximate reading of 10.15.
